name: Sawtelle Japantown
blurb: Japanese American gardeners settled here from 1910. By 1941 the neighborhood held 26 nurseries and eight boarding houses that worked as a gardeners' college. Los Angeles made the name official in 2015.

name: Little Tokyo
blurb: A National Historic District since 1986, and the home of the Japanese American National Museum.

name: Monterey Park
blurb: The center of the San Gabriel Valley's Chinese American community since the 1970s.

name: Alhambra
blurb: Sits next to Monterey Park in the stretch of the San Gabriel Valley people call the 626.

name: Historic Filipinotown
blurb: Named by Los Angeles City Council in 2002, along the stretch of Temple Street west of Echo Park.

name: Koreatown
blurb: The densest neighborhood in Los Angeles, and the largest Korean community outside Korea.

name: Torrance
blurb: The South Bay's Japanese American center, anchored by the Japanese corporate offices that moved here from the 1970s.

name: Cerritos
blurb: One of the most ethnically diverse cities in the country, with no single majority group.

name: Little Saigon
blurb: The largest Vietnamese community outside Vietnam, spread across Westminster and Garden Grove.

name: Japantown, San Francisco
blurb: One of three Japantowns left in the United States. The other two are in San Jose and Los Angeles.

name: Japantown, San Jose
blurb: The only Japantown in the country that has never been displaced from its original blocks.

name: Chinatown, Manhattan
blurb: The largest concentration of Chinese people in the Western Hemisphere.

name: Chinatown-International District
blurb: Seattle's Chinese, Japanese, Filipino and Vietnamese communities share one historic district.
